message.content:
For an ideal, fair coin each flip has two equally likely outcomes—heads or tails.  
Thus  

\[
P(\text{head})=\frac{\text{number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{total possible outcomes}}
               = \frac{1}{2}=0.50 .
\]

If you have evidence that the coin might be biased, you'd need additional information (e.g., observed frequencies from many flips) to estimate \(P(\text{head})\).
